summary: Catalog backend largely matches TD. SQL is fully parameterized, pagination bounds enforced, admin endpoints behind JWT middleware (with handler-level role re-check as defense-in-depth), outbox INSERT is correctly co-located in a pgx.Tx with the products INSERT, and partial indexes from TD are present in migrations. No critical security findings. Two functional gaps and several mediums to fix before merge: outbox relay goroutine lacks panic-recovery (one panic kills the whole service); product.detail admin-visibility path is dead code (claims never populated on the public route, so DELETED/DRAFT can never be seen by admin via this endpoint — safe direction, but contract behavior unmet); FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED comment is misleading (lock is released when rows close, not held through MarkPublished — at-least-once is still satisfied, but the comment overstates the guarantee); category.* and product.update/soft-delete are stubs returning 501 (expected per MVP, but ensure run-log captures this so the QA stage doesn't treat 501 as a regression).

findings.title: Outbox relay goroutine lacks panic recovery — one panic crashes the whole service
findings.evidence: backend/services/catalog/main.go lines 82, 113-134. `go startOutboxRelay(...)` is started without a deferred recover. main.go's defer recover() at line 91-95 covers ListenAndServe in the main goroutine only — it does NOT cover the relay goroutine. A panic inside relayTick (e.g., nil pgx pool, malformed JSON path that future code reaches, kafka producer panic) will kill the entire process. Gin's gin.Recovery() only protects HTTP handler goroutines.
findings.abuse_case: A malformed payload_json row or a transient pgx pool nil-deref triggers a panic in the relay; the entire HTTP server is killed; storefront browsing goes down even though no HTTP traffic was the trigger.
findings.validation: Unit test: inject a producer that panics on first Send; assert the goroutine logs and recovers, next tick proceeds. Integration: run service, kill kafka mid-tick, assert HTTP server stays up.
findings.residual_risk: After fix, a recovered panic still loses the in-flight batch (rows remain pending, retried next tick — correct at-least-once).

findings.title: product.detail admin-visibility branch is dead code — DELETED/DRAFT path unreachable for admins
findings.evidence: backend/services/catalog/app/catalog/handler_product_detail.go lines 132-153. extractIsAdmin calls token.ClaimsFromContext(c.Request.Context()) — but product.detail is registered in the public route group (router.go lines 50-56) which has NO JWT middleware in the chain, so claims are never set in the request context. The function then returns false on the err path without ever attempting raw-token verification. Net behavior: every caller — even with a valid ADMIN bearer token — is treated as non-admin. DELETED/DRAFT products always return 404.
findings.stride: Spoofing/Information Disclosure inverse — currently FAILS-CLOSED (good), but contract behavior is unmet.
findings.abuse_case: Inverse: the security-positive direction holds — non-admins cannot see DELETED records via product.detail. The functional gap is that admins also can't, so the documented admin path (TD product.detail.auth_notes lines 175-176) doesn't work. PR-014 / CAT-009 advisory honored: Order does NOT call back to Catalog for DELETED — confirmed elsewhere — so this dead branch causes no leak today.
findings.fix:
Two options:
  (a) Per TD intent, do raw verification of the Authorization header on the public route when present. Use common/token.NewJWTVerifier — same key as admin group. Reject malformed signature silently (return false). Only set isAdmin=true on a fully verified ADMIN token.
  (b) Simpler: add a separate /api/v1/catalog/admin/product/detail route inside the JWT middleware group; let the public detail strictly return 404 for DELETED/DRAFT. This avoids signature-verification on a public path and matches the L0 critique's preference for explicit admin endpoints.
Recommend (b) for MVP — minimal diff, clear blast radius, no signature-verify on public path.
findings.validation: Integration test: ADMIN token + DELETED productId on public detail → 404 (current behavior, codify it). On the new admin detail route → full record. CUSTOMER token on admin detail → 403.
findings.residual_risk: After fix-(b), admin-only fields are reachable only through an authenticated ADMIN route; public detail is leak-proof by construction.

findings.title: Outbox FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lock does not span until MarkPublished — comment is misleading
findings.evidence: backend/services/catalog/app/catalog/access/storage_outbox.go lines 52-79 (FetchPending) and 82-96 (MarkPublished). The pgx pool's Query checks out a connection, runs SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and returns the connection to the pool when rows.Close() runs (defer at line 68). The transaction implicit in that single query commits on connection return, releasing the row locks. MarkPublished then runs on a fresh connection. Therefore the lock does NOT prevent a second relay instance from re-fetching and re-publishing the same rows during the window between Kafka ACK and MarkPublished. At-least-once semantics still hold (TD line 100 acknowledges this and requires consumer dedup on eventId), so this is not a correctness defect — but the code reads as if FOR UPDATE provides cross-call isolation, which it does not.
findings.stride: Repudiation (weakly — duplicate event publish if relay is run with N>1 replicas)
findings.abuse_case: Operator scales catalog to 2 replicas (both run the relay). Replica A SELECTs+ACKs Kafka, before MarkPublished runs; Replica B SELECTs the same row (lock is gone), publishes again. Inventory consumer dedups on eventId. No corruption; observable as duplicate Kafka writes.
findings.fix:
Either (preferred) explicitly run FetchPending + MarkPublished in a single tx to make the comment true:
  tx, _ := s.db.Begin(ctx)
  defer tx.Rollback(ctx)
  rows := tx.Query(... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ...)
  // process each row, send to Kafka
  tx.Exec("UPDATE ... SET published_at=NOW() WHERE id=ANY($1)", ids)
  tx.Commit(ctx)
— or fix the comment to state at-least-once with consumer dedup. Recommend the tx-spanning fix because it is cheap and matches TD's stated intent. Note: holding a tx across Kafka send increases lock duration; bound batchSize=100 keeps it small.
findings.validation: Integration: run two relay instances against same DB, assert Kafka receives each row exactly once (or at most twice — current) versus exactly once (after fix).
findings.residual_risk: After tx-spanning fix, lock held during Kafka send — slow Kafka can stall row processing. Existing 5s tick interval and 100-row batch keep this bounded.

findings.title: ADMIN role check is duplicated in every handler instead of centralized in middleware
findings.evidence: router/router.go lines 64-82: adminGroup uses middleware.JWT(parser, verifier) which (per common/middleware) typically only verifies signature/issuer/audience. Each handler (e.g., handler_product_create.go lines 56-64) re-reads claims.Extra["role"] and 403s if not ADMIN. This works — defense in depth — but a future admin endpoint added to adminGroup that forgets the role check will accept any valid JWT (including CUSTOMER).
findings.abuse_case: A new admin endpoint is added (e.g., a future bulk-import) and the developer forgets the role guard. CUSTOMER tokens succeed silently.
findings.fix:
Add a thin RequireRole("ADMIN") middleware in common/middleware (or local to catalog) and chain it after JWT on adminGroup:
  adminGroup.Use(middleware.JWT(parser, verifier), middleware.RequireRole("ADMIN"))
Then remove the per-handler role-check duplication (keep claims.Sub extraction for actor_user_id).
findings.validation: Add a regression test that a CUSTOMER token is rejected at middleware before any handler runs (assert handler counter does not increment).
findings.residual_risk: Centralization removes the by-handler footgun; remaining risk is middleware-ordering mistakes, which are now a single review point.

findings.title: main.go `defer recover` for HTTP server prints rec without stack — debug-unfriendly
findings.evidence: main.go lines 91-95. recover() is logged but runtime/debug.Stack() is not captured. For a panic in production, root-causing without the stack is hard.
findings.fix: Capture and log debug.Stack() alongside the panic value: slog.Error("HTTP server panicked", "panic", rec, "stack", string(debug.Stack())).
findings.validation: Force a panic in a test handler; assert the log line carries a non-empty stack.

findings.title: extractSKU swallows JSON-unmarshal errors silently → loss of partition-key observability
findings.evidence: main.go lines 194-201. If payload_json is malformed (which would itself indicate a corrupt write), Kafka receives the message with empty partition key (round-robin), and there is no log line. No metric increments either.
findings.fix: Log a warn with outbox_id when the payload cannot be parsed: slog.Warn("outbox relay: payload missing sku — partition key empty", "outbox_id", row.ID).
findings.validation: Insert a malformed payload row in test; relay tick produces a warn line and still publishes the event.

findings.title: ProductCreate uses fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", float64) for money — float64 not safe for monetary precision
findings.evidence: handler_product_create.go line 107 and handler_product_list.go line 237 (formatDecimal). The product_create request type is `Price float64`. Float64 cannot represent THB 0.01 cleanly; %.2f rounds half-to-even, which is acceptable for THB (no sub-cent), but the JSON ingress is still float64 — a price of 19.99 may arrive as 19.989999... and round-trip to "19.99" by luck. For a B2C catalog at THB granularity this is acceptable, but for any future jurisdiction with sub-cent rounding rules it will silently drift.
findings.fix: Bind price as json.Number or string at the request DTO; parse with shopspring/decimal.NewFromString; reject anything with > 2 decimal places. Pattern matches the access layer which already stores price as string. Defer if MVP scope requires float64 — note in the README and in residual risk.
findings.validation: Property test: prices in {0.01, 0.05, 19.99, 12345.67, 9999999.99} round-trip exactly through create→detail.
findings.residual_risk: After fix, rounding is bit-exact. Current state is acceptable at THB MVP scale.

findings.title: slog.Info on product create logs sku and product_id — confirm SKU is not classified PII per data-classification
findings.evidence: service.go line 265: slog.Info("product created", "product_id", productID, "sku", input.SKU, "status", input.Status). SKU is product metadata, not customer PII — generally fine. Flagging only because TD does not include a logged-fields allowlist; explicit confirmation is cheap.
findings.fix: Add a one-line note in README.md or a logging.md confirming SKU/productID/status are NOT PII and may be logged at INFO. Re-check at the cross-cutting `logging` review when sec-rev-l3 runs.

findings.title: category.list public route accepts activeOnly=false from any caller — informational exposure
findings.evidence: router.go line 60 — categoryGroup.POST("/list", ...) is in publicGroup. Per TD ambiguity item line 685-688, this is a known accepted MVP limitation. Currently the handler is a 501 stub so non-issue today; gating is needed before unlocking the real handler.
findings.fix: When implementing category.list, either (a) ignore activeOnly=false from non-admin callers (force true), or (b) split into public /category/list (active only) and admin /admin/category/list (full). Recommended (a) for MVP; document.
findings.validation: Integration: public caller passing activeOnly=false receives only active categories.
findings.residual_risk: Inactive categories are not sensitive; impact bounded to UX-leak.

findings.title: Partial indexes per TD PERF-001 are present in migrations
findings.evidence: migrations/002_create_products.up.sql lines 22-35 — idx_products_listing, idx_products_price, idx_products_created all created with WHERE status='ACTIVE' AND visible=TRUE; matches td.json indexes block lines 47-52.
findings.validation: After seeding 1k rows, EXPLAIN ANALYZE the product.list query path; expect index scans on the partial indexes.

findings.title: Outbox-tx atomicity is correctly implemented via pgx.Tx
findings.evidence: service.go lines 179-263 — tx := s.db.Begin(ctx); deferred Rollback on error; products.Insert + product_images.Insert + product_status_history.Insert + outbox_events.Insert all use the same `tx` Querier; Commit only after all four succeed. ProductStorage.Insert/InsertStatusHistory and ImageStorage.Insert and OutboxStorage.Insert all accept a Querier (interface satisfied by both *pgxpool.Pool and pgx.Tx, see storage_product.go lines 116-120) — confirmed they will execute on the passed tx, not a separate pool connection.
findings.validation: Integration: simulate a duplicate-SKU; assert no row appears in outbox_events nor in product_status_history (full rollback). Already in test_strategy.
findings.residual_risk: None — pattern matches TD edge_behavior line 274.

findings.title: product.list parameterized SQL — confirmed, no string concatenation
findings.evidence: storage_product.go lines 179-206 — baseWhere uses $1..$4 for filter values; ORDER BY is built via buildOrderClause switch over a validated SortOption enum (lines 324-337); LIMIT/OFFSET via $6/$7. ILIKE search uses '%'||$4||'%' which keeps $4 a parameter (Postgres concatenation happens server-side after parameter binding — safe). No fmt.Sprintf, no string-format, no caller-controlled SQL. Same pattern in storage_outbox.go (FOR UPDATE LIMIT $1) and storage_image.go.
findings.validation: Static: gosec G201/G202 should pass clean on this package.

checked_axes.product_list_filter_sql_parameterized: PASS — $1..$7 only; ORDER BY from validated enum
checked_axes.admin_endpoints_jwt_middleware: PASS — adminGroup behind middleware.JWT; handler re-checks role (medium: centralize to middleware)
checked_axes.outbox_tx_atomicity: PASS — single pgx.Tx covers products + images + status_history + outbox INSERTs
checked_axes.deleted_product_leak_via_detail: PASS — fails-closed (admin path is dead code, returns 404 for DELETED/DRAFT to all callers); functional fix needed
checked_axes.order_no_callback_for_deleted: PASS — confirmed by td.json product.soft-delete edge_behavior; no Catalog→Order coupling for DELETED
checked_axes.public_admin_route_grouping: PASS — public group has no JWT; admin group has JWT
checked_axes.performance_indexes_present: PASS — partial indexes per TD PERF-001 in migrations/002
